review.review: The living hero exhausted the planner, not the game clock. Bookshelf 635 first appears at decision 347 (line 1074); shelves 636–638 follow at decision 348 (line 1077). The policy reserves liquid flame for every bookshelf, but its unknown-fire preparation admits barricades, not shelves. Hungry room preparation also declines. The last scroll publicly becomes Remove Curse, not Identify. Decision 354's accepted cancellation advances time; decision 355 (line 1093) terminates because the sole missing supply is flame at 635. Source-pinned offline bookkeeping reconstruction matches all 355 selected actions, reasons, intents and controllers and the exact terminal blocker; this is reconstructed state, not recorded memory. It excludes active retrievals and competing room demands. Ordinary test banks exist, but they do not override supply preservation or establish safe testing and retrieval. No patch is submitted: shelf-back cells 599–602 remain unobserved, and no known identification or reconnaissance resource remains. The game source permits both ordinary library shelves and flame-separated rewards, so dropping reservation or extending unknown-fire use would lack safety evidence. The unchanged source passes 1,849 unit tests, with four skipped; no candidate red/green validation is claimed.
review.learnings: Treat bookshelf-driven supply exhaustion as an obligation/admission mismatch, not a death or a reason to wait longer. Preserve unknown potion identities and mandatory pickups. A safe repair needs positive public evidence distinguishing optional shelf fuel from a real retrieval barrier, or executable nonconsumptive reconnaissance; an ordinary safe test bank alone is insufficient.

Establish a positive public-evidence distinction while retaining reservation for unknown backs and real retrievals; otherwise establish an executable nonconsumptive reconnaissance plan before changing arbitration.
